paragraph.text: I36. "Feeding a dog or cat vegan food is animal abuse"

the answer is different for dogs and cats. Dogs are omnivores, and in 2024 the British Veterinary Association recognized that they can be fed a vegan diet, as long as it is nutritionally complete and monitored by a vet. Cats are obligate carnivores, and the same association still advises against a vegan diet for them; the studies that exist rely on guardians' reports. Most importantly, the difficulty of feeding a cat doesn't change the question about the human plate: people can live well without eating animals.

Each animal needs the right food for them. Dogs can eat food without meat, if it has everything they need and a vet keeps an eye on them. Cats are different and need special care. What matters is that the animal stays healthy, and that people, who can live well without meat, do their part.

It depends on the species. Dogs are omnivores, and in 2024 the British Veterinary Association recognized that they can live on a complete vegan diet, with veterinary monitoring. Cats are obligate carnivores, and the same association advises against a vegan diet for them. A poorly planned home-made diet is risky for both. And none of this changes the question for people: we can live well without eating animals.

text.bold: 2. The veterinary position has changed for dogs.

paragraph.text: In 2024, the British Veterinary Association recognized that dogs can be fed nutritionally complete vegan diets, warning about the lack of long-term data and recommending monitoring.
A 2022 survey of 2,536 dogs, published in

, found equal or better health indicators in dogs on vegan diets, but the data come from the guardians themselves. A similar 2023 study of cats found no significant difference in the general indicators, with the same limitation and only 127 cats on vegan diets.

The nutrients cats need can be produced synthetically, but evidence of long-term safety is weak, and the main veterinary bodies advise against it. Anyone who wants to try should use only a complete commercial food and veterinary monitoring. A home-made meat-free diet for cats is risky.
Conventional pet foods use meat and by-products from animals who were bred and slaughtered. The dilemma is real for anyone living with a cat, and there is no answer without a cost.

text.bold: The difficulty with cats doesn't extend to people.

paragraph.text: Humans aren't obligate carnivores, and can live well without eating animals.

The question of what to feed companion animals is hard, especially for cats. But it doesn't answer the main question: whether we, who can live well without eating animals, have a reason to keep doing so.

It's true that dogs and cats have their own needs, that poorly planned home-made diets are dangerous, and that for cats the evidence on vegan diets is weak and caution is justified.
But for dogs there are complete foods accepted by veterinary bodies, and the difficulty with cats changes nothing about the human plate.
